source.text: וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב עַל־יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּב֤וֹא גַֽם־הַשָּׂטָן֙ בְּתֹכָ֔ם לְהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב עַל־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was the day, and came [the] sons of God to present themselves before YHWH, and came also the satan in their midst to present himself before YHWH.

en.L: And the day came when the sons of God came to present themselves before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the satan also came among them to present himself before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: On another day the sons of God came to present themselves before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the Accuser also came among them to present himself before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: On another day the heavenly beings came to stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the Accuser came with them to stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} too.

es.L: Y llegó el día en que los hijos de Dios vinieron a presentarse delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y vino también el satán entre ellos a presentarse delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Otro día los hijos de Dios vinieron a presentarse ante {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y también el Acusador vino entre ellos a presentarse ante {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Otro día los seres celestiales vinieron a presentarse delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y el Acusador también vino con ellos a presentarse delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et le jour arriva où les fils de Dieu vinrent se présenter devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et le satan vint aussi parmi eux se présenter devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Un autre jour, les fils de Dieu vinrent se présenter devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et l’Accusateur vint lui aussi au milieu d’eux se présenter devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Un autre jour, les êtres célestes sont venus se tenir devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et l’Accusateur est venu avec eux pour se tenir lui aussi devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Na ikawa siku moja, wana wa Mungu walikuja kujisimamisha mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, naye yule satani akaja pia kati yao kujisimamisha mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Siku nyingine wana wa Mungu walikuja kusimama mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, na Mshtaki naye akaja pamoja nao kusimama mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Siku nyingine viumbe wa mbinguni walifika mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, na Mshtaki naye akaja pamoja nao kusimama mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Và đến ngày kia, các con trai của Đức Chúa Trời đến trình diện trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và kẻ sa-tan cũng đến giữa họ để trình diện trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Một ngày khác, các con trai của Đức Chúa Trời lại đến trình diện trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và Kẻ Tố Cáo cũng đến giữa họ để trình diện trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Một ngày khác, các đấng ở trên trời đến đứng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và Kẻ Tố Cáo cũng đến với họ để đứng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그날이 되어, 하나님의 아들들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 나아와 서려고 왔고, 그 사탄도 그들 가운데 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 나아와 서려고 왔다.
ko.B: 또 어느 날 하나님의 아들들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 나아와 자기 자리에 섰다. 고발자도 그들 가운데 함께 와서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 섰다.
ko.R: 또 어느 날 하늘의 존재들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 와서 섰다. 고발자도 그들과 함께 와서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 섰다.

decisions.choice: the scene of 1:6 repeated, with one addition
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 1:6 word for word and adds that the satan too came "to present himself before the LORD". This time he comes, like the others, to give his report, and the reader expects him to answer for the outcome of the first test.

decisions.choice: the sons of God; the satan: as at 1:6
decisions.reason: The sons of God are the heavenly beings of God's council, and "the satan" is a title, the accuser or adversary in the heavenly court; see the notes at 1:6.

decisions.choice: the satan (Literal), the Accuser (Balanced, Readable); the heavenly beings (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1:6. Balanced and Readable say "on another day" because this is a second scene of the same kind; Literal keeps "the day came".

decisions.choice: Narrative tenses: passé simple at Literal and Balanced, passé composé at Readable
decisions.reason: As in chapter 1: the prose of Job 1-2 uses the literary narrative tense at Literal and Balanced and the spoken past tense at Readable.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֔ן אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה תָּבֹ֑א וַיַּ֨עַן הַשָּׂטָ֤ן אֶת־יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר מִשֻּׁ֣ט בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמֵהִתְהַלֵּ֖ךְ בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said YHWH to the satan, where [is] this, from where do you come? And answered the satan YHWH and said, from roaming on the earth and from walking about on it.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to the satan, "Where is it you come from?" And the satan answered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "From roaming on the earth, and from walking about on it."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to the Accuser, "Where have you come from?" The Accuser answered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "From roaming the earth and walking up and down on it."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} asked the Accuser, "Where have you been?" The Accuser answered, "I have been going all over the earth, walking back and forth across it."

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo al satán: «¿De dónde, pues, vienes?». Y el satán respondió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y dijo: «De rondar por la tierra y de andar de un lado a otro por ella».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo al Acusador: «¿De dónde has venido?». El Acusador respondió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «De recorrer la tierra y andar de aquí para allá por ella».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le preguntó al Acusador: «¿Dónde has estado?». El Acusador respondió: «He estado recorriendo toda la tierra, yendo de un lado a otro».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit au satan : « D’où donc viens-tu ? » Et le satan répondit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et dit : « De rôder sur la terre et d’y circuler. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à l’Accusateur : « D’où viens-tu ? » L’Accusateur répondit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « De rôder sur la terre et d’y aller et venir. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a demandé à l’Accusateur : « Où étais-tu ? » L’Accusateur a répondu : « J’ai parcouru toute la terre, j’y suis allé de long en large. »

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia yule satani, "Je, unatoka wapi basi?" Naye yule satani akamjibu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akasema, "Kutoka kuranda-randa duniani, na kutembea-tembea juu yake."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Mshtaki, "Umetoka wapi?" Mshtaki akamjibu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Nimekuwa nikizurura duniani na kutembea juu na chini ndani yake."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwuliza Mshtaki, "Ulikuwa wapi?" Mshtaki akajibu, "Nimekuwa nikizunguka dunia yote, nikitembea huku na kule."

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với kẻ sa-tan: "Ngươi từ đâu mà đến?" Và kẻ sa-tan thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} rằng: "Từ việc lang thang trên đất và đi lại trên đó."
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán hỏi Kẻ Tố Cáo: "Ngươi từ đâu đến?" Kẻ Tố Cáo thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Tôi vừa rong ruổi khắp đất và đi tới đi lui trên đó."
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hỏi Kẻ Tố Cáo: "Ngươi đã ở đâu?" Kẻ Tố Cáo thưa: "Tôi đã đi khắp mặt đất, đi tới đi lui khắp nơi."

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 사탄에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 대체 어디에서 오느냐?" 그러자 그 사탄이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 대답하여 말했다. "땅 위를 두루 다니다가, 그 위를 거닐다가 왔습니다."
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 고발자에게 물으셨다. "어디에서 왔느냐?" 고발자가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 대답했다. "땅을 두루 돌아다니며 이리저리 거닐다가 왔습니다."
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 고발자에게 물으셨다. "어디에 있다 왔느냐?" 고발자가 대답했다. "온 땅을 돌아다녔습니다. 이곳저곳을 오가며 다녔습니다."

decisions.choice: where from?: a slightly different question from 1:7, with the same sense
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a different pair of words for "from where" than in 1:7 (as in Genesis 16:8), but the question is the same. The satan's answer is word for word that of 1:7; see the note there on roaming the earth.

decisions.choice: Where is it you come from? (Literal)
decisions.reason: Literal shows that the wording differs a little from 1:7; Balanced and Readable give the same English as there because the meaning is the same.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֗ן הֲשַׂ֣מְתָּ לִבְּךָ֮ אֶל־עַבְדִּ֣י אִיּוֹב֒ כִּי֩ אֵ֨ין כָּמֹ֜הוּ בָּאָ֗רֶץ אִ֣ישׁ תָּ֧ם וְיָשָׁ֛ר יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְסָ֣ר מֵרָ֑ע וְעֹדֶ֨נּוּ֙ מַחֲזִ֣יק בְּתֻמָּת֔וֹ וַתְּסִיתֵ֥נִי ב֖וֹ לְבַלְּע֥וֹ חִנָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said YHWH to the satan, have you set your heart on my servant Job? For there is none like him on the earth, a man blameless and upright, fearing God and turning aside from evil; and still he [is] holding fast to his integrity, and you incited me against him to swallow him up for nothing.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to the satan, "Have you set your heart on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave Job? For there is none like him on the earth, a man blameless and upright, who fears God and turns away from evil. And he still holds fast to his integrity, though you incited {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} against him to swallow him up for nothing."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to the Accuser, "Have you considered {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Job? There is no one like him on earth: a man blameless and upright, who fears God and turns away from evil. He still holds firmly to his integrity, even though you stirred {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} up against him to destroy him for no reason."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to the Accuser, "Have you noticed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Job? There is no one on earth like him. He is blameless and upright. He honors God and keeps away from evil. You urged {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to act against him and ruin him for no reason, but he still holds on to his integrity."

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo al satán: «¿Has puesto tu corazón en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} esclavo Job? Porque no hay nadie como él en la tierra, hombre íntegro y recto, que teme a Dios y se aparta del mal. Y todavía se aferra a su integridad, aunque tú {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} incitaste contra él para devorarlo por nada».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo al Acusador: «¿Te has fijado en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Job? No hay nadie como él en la tierra: es un hombre íntegro y recto, que teme a Dios y se aparta del mal. Todavía se mantiene firme en su integridad, aunque tú {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} provocaste contra él para destruirlo sin motivo».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo al Acusador: «¿Has notado a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Job? No hay nadie en la tierra como él. Es íntegro y recto. Honra a Dios y se aleja del mal. Tú {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} empujaste a actuar contra él y a arruinarlo sin motivo, pero él sigue aferrado a su integridad».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit au satan : « As-tu posé ton cœur sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} esclave Job ? Car il n’y a personne comme lui sur la terre, un homme intègre et droit, qui craint Dieu et se détourne du mal. Et il tient encore ferme son intégrité, alors que tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pressais contre lui de l’engloutir pour rien. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à l’Accusateur : « As-tu prêté attention à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Job ? Il n’a pas son pareil sur terre : c’est un homme intègre et droit, qui craint Dieu et se détourne du mal. Il reste ferme dans son intégrité, bien que tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} aies poussé contre lui pour le détruire sans raison. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à l’Accusateur : « As-tu vu {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Job ? Personne sur la terre ne lui ressemble. Il est intègre et droit. Il honore Dieu et se tient loin du mal. Tu es venu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pousser à agir contre lui et à le ruiner sans raison, mais il reste attaché à son intégrité. »

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia yule satani, "Je, umeweka moyo wako juu ya mtumwa {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Ayubu? Kwa maana hakuna aliye kama yeye duniani, mtu mkamilifu na mnyofu, anayemcha Mungu na kujiepusha na uovu. Naye bado anashikilia ukamilifu wake, ingawa ulinichochea dhidi yake nimmeze bure."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Mshtaki, "Je, umemfikiria mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Ayubu? Hakuna mtu kama yeye duniani: ni mtu mkamilifu na mnyofu, anayemcha Mungu na kujiepusha na uovu. Bado anashikilia kwa uthabiti ukamilifu wake, ingawa ulinichochea dhidi yake ili nimwangamize bila sababu."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Mshtaki, "Je, umemwona mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Ayubu? Hakuna mtu duniani aliye kama yeye. Yeye ni mkamilifu na mnyofu. Anamheshimu Mungu na kukaa mbali na uovu. Ulinishawishi nimshambulie na kumwangamiza bila sababu, lakini bado anashikilia ukamilifu wake."

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với kẻ sa-tan: "Ngươi có để lòng đến nô lệ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Gióp không? Vì trên đất không có ai như người, một người trọn vẹn và ngay thẳng, kính sợ Đức Chúa Trời và lánh xa điều ác. Người vẫn còn giữ vững sự trọn vẹn của mình, dù ngươi đã xúi giục {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chống lại người để nuốt người đi vô cớ."
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Kẻ Tố Cáo: "Ngươi có lưu tâm đến đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Gióp chăng? Trên đất chẳng có ai bằng người: một người trọn vẹn và ngay thẳng, kính sợ Đức Chúa Trời và lánh xa điều ác. Người vẫn bám chặt lấy sự trọn vẹn của mình, dù ngươi đã khích {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chống lại người để hủy diệt người vô cớ."
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Kẻ Tố Cáo: "Ngươi có thấy đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Gióp không? Trên đất không ai giống như người. Người trọn vẹn và ngay thẳng. Người tôn kính Đức Chúa Trời và tránh xa điều ác. Ngươi đã giục {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ra tay hại người và hủy hoại người vô cớ, nhưng người vẫn giữ vững sự trọn vẹn của mình."

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 사탄에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 내 종 욥에게 네 마음을 두었느냐? 땅 위에 그와 같은 자가 없으니, 흠 없고 정직하며, 하나님을 경외하고 악에서 떠난 사람이다. 그는 아직도 자기의 온전함을 굳게 붙들고 있다. 네가 나를 부추겨 까닭 없이 그를 삼키게 하였는데도 말이다."
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 고발자에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 내 종 욥을 눈여겨보았느냐? 땅 위에 그만한 사람이 없다. 그는 흠 없고 정직하며, 하나님을 경외하고 악에서 떠난 사람이다. 네가 나를 부추겨 아무 까닭 없이 그를 망하게 하였는데도, 그는 여전히 자기의 온전함을 굳게 지키고 있다."
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 고발자에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 내 종 욥을 보았느냐? 세상에 그런 사람은 없다. 그는 흠 없고 정직하다. 그는 하나님을 두려운 마음으로 섬기고 악한 일을 멀리한다. 너는 나를 졸라 아무 이유 없이 그를 치고 망하게 하였다. 그래도 그는 여전히 온전함을 지키고 있다."

decisions.choice: holds fast to his integrity: keeps his wholeness of heart toward God
decisions.reason: "Integrity" is the noun of the word "blameless" (1:1): wholeness, a life all of one piece. The phrase returns from his wife (2:9) and from Job himself: "till I die I will not put away my integrity from me" (27:5; also 31:6).

decisions.choice: for nothing: without cause
decisions.reason: This is the word the satan used in 1:9 ("Does Job fear God for nothing?"). The LORD turns it back on him: Job's devotion has proved to be "for nothing", not bought, while his ruin has been "for nothing", without any cause in Job.

decisions.choice: you incited me against him: the LORD speaks of the disaster as his own act
decisions.reason: The verb means to stir up, urge or entice someone to act (1 Samuel 26:19; 2 Samuel 24:1; 1 Kings 21:25). The LORD does not say the satan acted alone; he speaks of himself as having been moved against Job, just as Job said "the LORD has taken" (1:21). The text does not soften this, and the book does not explain it.

decisions.choice: to swallow him up: to destroy him
decisions.reason: "Swallow" is a common picture for destroying completely (2 Samuel 20:19-20; Lamentations 2:2, 5).

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1:8.

decisions.choice: the two clauses reversed (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable tells first what the Accuser did and then that Job still holds on, which makes the contrast plain in two short sentences.

decisions.choice: "integridad" at every level

source.text: וַיַּ֧עַן הַשָּׂטָ֛ן אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר ע֣וֹר בְּעַד־ע֗וֹר וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָאִ֔ישׁ יִתֵּ֖ן בְּעַ֥ד נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered the satan YHWH and said, skin for skin, and all that [is] to a man he will give for his life.

en.L: And the satan answered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "Skin for skin! And all that {{gender:a person has, they|a man has, he}} will give for {{gender:their|his}} life.
en.B: The Accuser answered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Skin for skin! {{gender:People|A man}} will give {{gender:everything they have|everything he has}} to save {{gender:their own lives|his own life}}.
en.R: The Accuser answered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "{{gender:People|A man}} will trade anything to save {{gender:their own skin|his own skin}}. {{gender:They|He}} will give up everything {{gender:they have|he has}} to stay alive.

es.L: Y el satán respondió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y dijo: «¡Piel por piel! Y todo lo que {{gender:la persona|el hombre}} tiene lo dará por su vida.
es.B: El Acusador respondió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «¡Piel por piel! {{gender:La persona|El hombre}} dará todo lo que tiene por salvar su propia vida.
es.R: El Acusador respondió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «Cualquiera da lo que sea por salvar el pellejo. Entrega todo lo que tiene con tal de seguir vivo.

fr.L: Et le satan répondit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et dit : « Peau pour peau ! Et tout ce qu’a {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}, il le donnera pour sa vie.
fr.B: L’Accusateur répondit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Peau pour peau ! {{gender:L’être humain|L’homme}} donnera tout ce qu’il possède pour sauver sa propre vie.
fr.R: L’Accusateur a répondu {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Pour sauver sa peau, on est prêt à tout donner. On abandonne tout ce qu’on a pour rester en vie.

sw.L: Naye yule satani akamjibu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akasema, "Ngozi kwa ngozi! Na vyote alivyo navyo mtu atavitoa kwa ajili ya uhai wake.
sw.B: Mshtaki akamjibu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Ngozi kwa ngozi! Mtu atatoa kila kitu alicho nacho ili kuokoa maisha yake mwenyewe.
sw.R: Mshtaki akamjibu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Mtu yuko tayari kutoa chochote ili kujiokoa. Ataacha kila kitu alicho nacho ili abaki hai.

vi.L: Và kẻ sa-tan thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} rằng: "Da thay cho da! Và tất cả những gì một người có, người sẽ đem cho để đổi lấy mạng sống mình.
vi.B: Kẻ Tố Cáo thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Da thay cho da! Người ta sẵn sàng đưa ra mọi thứ mình có để giữ lấy mạng sống.
vi.R: Kẻ Tố Cáo thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Để giữ lấy mạng mình, người ta chịu đổi bất cứ thứ gì. Người ta sẽ bỏ hết mọi thứ mình có để được sống.

ko.L: 그러자 그 사탄이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 대답하여 말했다. "가죽에는 가죽입니다! 사람은 자기에게 있는 모든 것을 자기 목숨을 위하여 내줄 것입니다.
ko.B: 고발자가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 대답했다. "가죽에는 가죽입니다! 사람은 제 목숨을 건지려고 가진 것을 다 내놓습니다.
ko.R: 고발자가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 대답했다. "사람은 제 목숨을 지키려고 무엇이든 내줍니다. 살아남기 위해서라면 가진 것을 모두 버립니다.

decisions.choice: skin for skin: a saying about exchange, that a person will give anything to save himself
decisions.reason: This proverb appears only here and its exact picture is not known. It may come from trade, one skin or hide given in exchange for another, meaning a person will pay any price for what matters to him. Some take it to mean that a person will give up the skin of others, even his children's, to save his own. Either way the second half explains it: a man will give everything he has for his life. The satan claims Job has so far lost only what is outside him.

decisions.choice: all that a man has he will give for his life: anyone, not a particular man
decisions.reason: "A man" here is anyone; the satan states a general rule about human beings. "Life" is the person's own living self, which the LORD later tells the satan to spare (2:6).

decisions.choice: gender span for the general "a man"
decisions.reason: The saying is about people in general, so the default is inclusive, with "a man" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: save their own skin (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the English idiom "to save one's own skin", which gives the sense of the proverb without its unfamiliar picture. The speech continues into the next verse, so the quotation is closed there.

decisions.choice: gender span "la persona" / "el hombre" (L, B); "cualquiera" with no span (R)
alternatives: A span at Readable as well
decisions.reason: The saying is about anyone; Spanish needs a noun for it at Literal and Balanced, where the setting offers the traditional "el hombre". Readable's "cualquiera" already includes everyone, so it has one wording.

decisions.choice: gender span "l'être humain" / "l'homme" (L, B); "on" with no span (R)
alternatives: A span at Readable as well
decisions.reason: The saying is about anyone; French needs a noun at Literal and Balanced, where the setting offers the traditional "l'homme". Readable's "on" already includes everyone, so it has one wording; the agreeing pronoun "il" stays outside the span, as French spans never cover pronouns.

decisions.choice: "mtu" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Mtu" means any human being, man or woman, so Swahili has one wording where English has two.

decisions.choice: "một người", "người ta" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người" is any human being, so there is one wording where English has two.

decisions.choice: "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" is any human being, so there is one wording where English has two.

records.literal_gloss: But stretch out, please, your hand and touch to his bone and to his flesh; if not to your face he will bless you.

en.L: But stretch out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand, please, and touch his bone and his flesh, [and see] if he will not curse {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face!"
en.B: But stretch out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand and strike his bone and his flesh, and he will surely curse {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face."
en.R: But reach out and hurt his body. Then he will curse {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face!"

fr.L: Mais étends donc {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main et touche à ses os et à sa chair, [et tu verras] s’il ne {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} maudit pas à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} face ! »
fr.B: Mais étends {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main et frappe-le dans ses os et dans sa chair : il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} maudira sûrement en face. »

sw.R: Lakini nyoosha mkono uudhuru mwili wake. Hapo ndipo atakulaani waziwazi!"

vi.L: Nhưng xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hãy giơ tay ra và đụng đến xương thịt người, [xem] người có nguyền rủa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngay trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không!"

vi.R: Nhưng xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hãy ra tay làm hại thân thể người. Rồi người sẽ nguyền rủa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngay trước mặt!"

ko.B: 그러나 주님께서 손을 펴서 그의 뼈와 살을 치시면, 그는 틀림없이 주님 앞에서 대놓고 주님을 저주할 것입니다."
ko.R: 그러나 주님께서 손을 뻗어 그의 몸을 쳐 보십시오. 그러면 그는 주님 앞에서 대놓고 주님을 저주할 것입니다!"

decisions.choice: his bone and his flesh: his body, his very self
decisions.reason: Bone and flesh together mean the whole body, the person himself (Genesis 2:23; 29:14). Having lost what he owned, Job is now to be struck in his own body.

decisions.choice: if he will not curse you: an oath, with "bless" meaning "curse"
decisions.reason: As in 1:11: "if not" makes a strong claim (he surely will), and the verb for "bless" stands in place of "curse" (see 1:5).

decisions.choice: reach out and hurt his body (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "stretch out your hand and touch his bone and his flesh" means.

records.literal_gloss: And said YHWH to the satan, see, he [is] in your hand; only his life preserve.

en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to the Accuser, "Very well, he is in your power. Only spare his life."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to the Accuser, "All right. You may do what you want to him. But you must not kill him."

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo al satán: «Mira, él está en tu mano; solo guarda su vida».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo al Acusador: «Está bien, él está en tu poder. Solo respeta su vida».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo al Acusador: «De acuerdo. Puedes hacer con él lo que quieras. Pero no lo mates».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit au satan : « Voici, il est dans ta main ; seulement, garde sa vie. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à l’Accusateur : « Soit ! Il est en ton pouvoir. Seulement, épargne sa vie. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à l’Accusateur : « D’accord. Tu peux faire de lui ce que tu veux. Mais tu ne dois pas le tuer. »

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia yule satani, "Tazama, yeye yumo mkononi mwako; ila uhai wake uuhifadhi."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Mshtaki, "Haya, yuko katika uwezo wako. Ila usiuguse uhai wake."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Mshtaki, "Sawa. Unaweza kumfanya lolote unalotaka. Lakini usimwue."

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với kẻ sa-tan: "Kìa, người ở trong tay ngươi; chỉ hãy giữ lấy mạng sống người."
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Kẻ Tố Cáo: "Được, người ở trong quyền ngươi. Chỉ phải để cho người sống."
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Kẻ Tố Cáo: "Được thôi. Ngươi muốn làm gì người cũng được. Nhưng ngươi không được giết người."

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 사탄에게 말씀하셨다. "보아라, 그가 네 손에 있다. 다만 그의 목숨은 지켜라."
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 고발자에게 말씀하셨다. "좋다. 그를 네 권한에 맡긴다. 다만 그의 목숨만은 살려 두어라."
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 고발자에게 말씀하셨다. "좋다. 그를 네가 원하는 대로 해도 된다. 그러나 그를 죽여서는 안 된다."

decisions.choice: only preserve his life: a new limit, still set by the LORD
decisions.reason: As in 1:12, the LORD grants the satan power but fixes a boundary. Before, it was Job's person; now it is his life. Job must live through the test.

decisions.choice: in your hand: in your power
decisions.reason: As in 1:12.

decisions.choice: preserve (Literal); spare (Balanced); must not kill him (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb means to keep or guard; Balanced and Readable say what guarding his life means here.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵא֙ הַשָּׂטָ֔ן מֵאֵ֖ת פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּ֤ךְ אֶת־אִיּוֹב֙ בִּשְׁחִ֣ין רָ֔ע מִכַּ֥ף רַגְל֖וֹ וְעַ֥ד קָדְקֳדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out the satan from with [the] face of YHWH, and struck Job with sores bad from [the] sole of his foot and to the crown of his head.

en.L: And the satan went out from the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and struck Job with bad sores from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.
en.B: So the Accuser went out from the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and struck Job with painful sores from the soles of his feet to the top of his head.
en.R: So the Accuser left the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and made painful sores break out all over Job's body, from the bottoms of his feet to the top of his head.

es.B: Así que el Acusador salió de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} e hirió a Job con llagas dolorosas desde la planta de los pies hasta la cabeza.
es.R: Así que el Acusador se retiró de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} e hizo que le salieran a Job llagas dolorosas por todo el cuerpo, desde la planta de los pies hasta la cabeza.

fr.L: Et le satan sortit de devant la face {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et il frappa Job de mauvais ulcères, de la plante de son pied jusqu’au sommet de son crâne.
fr.B: L’Accusateur se retira donc de la présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et frappa Job de plaies douloureuses, de la plante des pieds jusqu’au haut de la tête.
fr.R: L’Accusateur a donc quitté la présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et il a fait sortir des plaies douloureuses sur tout le corps de Job, du dessous des pieds jusqu’au haut de la tête.

sw.L: Naye yule satani akatoka mbele ya uso wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akampiga Ayubu kwa vidonda vibaya kuanzia nyayo za mguu wake mpaka kilele cha kichwa chake.
sw.B: Basi Mshtaki akaondoka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akampiga Ayubu kwa vidonda vyenye maumivu kuanzia nyayo za miguu hadi utosini.
sw.R: Basi Mshtaki akaondoka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akamletea Ayubu vidonda vyenye maumivu mwili mzima, kuanzia chini ya nyayo zake hadi juu ya kichwa chake.

vi.L: Và kẻ sa-tan đi ra khỏi trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và giáng cho Gióp những ung nhọt độc từ lòng bàn chân người cho đến đỉnh đầu người.
vi.B: Vậy Kẻ Tố Cáo lui ra khỏi trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và giáng cho Gióp những ung nhọt đau đớn từ lòng bàn chân cho đến đỉnh đầu.
vi.R: Vậy Kẻ Tố Cáo rời khỏi trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và làm cho Gióp nổi ung nhọt đau đớn khắp người, từ lòng bàn chân đến tận đỉnh đầu.

ko.L: 그리고 그 사탄이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 얼굴 앞에서 나가서, 욥의 발바닥부터 머리 꼭대기까지 나쁜 종기로 욥을 쳤다.
ko.B: 그래서 고발자는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 물러가, 욥의 발바닥에서 머리끝까지 고통스러운 종기가 돋게 했다.
ko.R: 그래서 고발자는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 떠나가 욥의 온몸에, 발바닥부터 머리 꼭대기까지 아픈 종기가 생기게 했다.

decisions.choice: bad sores: inflamed boils on the skin
decisions.reason: The word names boils or inflamed sores (Exodus 9:9-11; Leviticus 13:18-20; 2 Kings 20:7). The disease cannot be identified. Job later describes its effects: itching, crusted and broken skin, sleeplessness and wasting (2:8; 7:4-5; 19:20; 30:17, 30).

decisions.choice: from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head: the words of the covenant curse
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 28:35 threatens the disobedient with "bad sores ... from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head", the same words. Anyone who knew that passage would take Job's disease as a sign of God's judgment, as his friends will; the reader knows that Job is blameless (2:3).

decisions.choice: made painful sores break out all over Job's body (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "all over Job's body" to make the extent plain before the phrase that spells it out.

source.text: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ל֣וֹ חֶ֔רֶשׂ לְהִתְגָּרֵ֖ד בּ֑וֹ וְה֖וּא יֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּתוֹךְ־הָאֵֽפֶר׃

en.B: Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself with as he sat among the ashes.
en.R: Job sat down in the ashes. He took a piece of a broken pot and used it to scratch his sores.

es.L: Y tomó para sí un tiesto para rascarse con él, y estaba sentado en medio de la ceniza.
es.B: Job tomó un trozo de vasija rota para rascarse mientras estaba sentado entre la ceniza.
es.R: Job se sentó en la ceniza. Tomó un pedazo de una olla rota y lo usaba para rascarse las llagas.

fr.L: Et il prit pour lui un tesson pour se gratter avec, et il était assis au milieu de la cendre.
fr.B: Job prit un débris de poterie pour se gratter, tandis qu’il était assis dans la cendre.
fr.R: Job s’est assis dans la cendre. Il a pris un morceau de pot cassé et s’en est servi pour gratter ses plaies.

sw.L: Naye akajitwalia kigae ili ajikune nacho, naye alikuwa ameketi katikati ya majivu.
sw.B: Ayubu akachukua kipande cha chungu kilichovunjika ili ajikune nacho alipokuwa ameketi katikati ya majivu.
sw.R: Ayubu aliketi chini kwenye majivu. Akachukua kipande cha chungu kilichovunjika, akakitumia kujikuna vidonda vyake.

vi.L: Và ông lấy cho mình một mảnh sành để gãi mình, và ông ngồi giữa đống tro.
vi.B: Gióp lấy một mảnh gốm vỡ để gãi mình trong khi ngồi giữa tro.
vi.R: Gióp ngồi trong đống tro. Ông lấy một mảnh nồi vỡ để gãi các chỗ ung nhọt.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 자기 몸을 긁으려고 질그릇 조각 하나를 집어 들었고, 잿더미 가운데 앉아 있었다.
ko.B: 욥은 깨진 질그릇 조각을 가져다 몸을 긁으며 잿더미 가운데 앉아 있었다.
ko.R: 욥은 잿더미에 주저앉았다. 그리고 깨진 그릇 조각을 집어 들고 종기 난 데를 긁었다.

decisions.choice: sitting among the ashes: a sign of grief and humiliation, perhaps on the town's ash heap
decisions.reason: Sitting in ashes or dust was a sign of mourning and deep humiliation (Jonah 3:6; Ezekiel 27:30; Job 42:6). The place may have been the heap outside the town where ashes and refuse were dumped (compare 1 Samuel 2:8; Psalm 113:7); the old Greek translation says Job sat "on the dung heap outside the city". The Hebrew says only "among the ashes".

decisions.choice: a potsherd to scrape himself: a broken piece of pottery, used against the itching sores
decisions.reason: Broken pottery lay everywhere in an ancient town. Job uses a shard to scrape his inflamed skin, a picture of pain and of how far the greatest man of the East has fallen (1:3).

decisions.choice: the sitting told first (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable puts Job's sitting in the ashes first and makes it a separate sentence, because the Hebrew clause describes where he already was.

source.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ עֹדְךָ֖ מַחֲזִ֣יק בְּתֻמָּתֶ֑ךָ בָּרֵ֥ךְ אֱלֹהִ֖ים וָמֻֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him his wife, still you [are] holding fast to your integrity? Bless God and die.

en.L: And his wife said to him, "Are you still holding fast to your integrity? Curse God and die!"
en.B: His wife said to him, "Are you still holding on to your integrity? Curse God and die!"
en.R: Job's wife said to him, "Are you still holding on to your integrity? Curse God and die!"

es.L: Y su mujer le dijo: «¿Todavía te aferras a tu integridad? ¡Maldice a Dios y muérete!».
es.B: Su esposa le dijo: «¿Todavía te mantienes firme en tu integridad? ¡Maldice a Dios y muérete!».
es.R: La esposa de Job le dijo: «¿Todavía sigues aferrado a tu integridad? ¡Maldice a Dios y muérete!».

fr.L: Et sa femme lui dit : « Tiens-tu encore ferme ton intégrité ? Maudis Dieu, et meurs ! »
fr.B: Sa femme lui dit : « Tu t’accroches encore à ton intégrité ? Maudis Dieu, et meurs ! »
fr.R: La femme de Job lui a dit : « Tu tiens encore à ton intégrité ? Maudis Dieu, et meurs ! »

sw.L: Na mkewe akamwambia, "Je, ungali unashikilia ukamilifu wako? Mlaani Mungu, ufe!"
sw.B: Mkewe akamwambia, "Je, bado unashikilia ukamilifu wako? Mlaani Mungu ufe!"
sw.R: Mke wa Ayubu akamwambia, "Bado unang'ang'ania ukamilifu wako? Mlaani Mungu ufe!"

vi.L: Và vợ ông nói với ông: "Ông vẫn còn giữ vững sự trọn vẹn của ông sao? Hãy nguyền rủa Đức Chúa Trời và chết đi!"
vi.B: Vợ ông nói với ông: "Anh vẫn còn bám lấy sự trọn vẹn của anh sao? Hãy nguyền rủa Đức Chúa Trời rồi chết đi!"
vi.R: Vợ Gióp nói với ông: "Anh vẫn còn giữ sự trọn vẹn của mình sao? Hãy nguyền rủa Đức Chúa Trời rồi chết đi!"

ko.L: 그리고 그의 아내가 그에게 말했다. "당신은 아직도 당신의 온전함을 굳게 붙들고 있어요? 하나님을 저주하고 죽어요!"
ko.B: 그의 아내가 그에게 말했다. "당신은 아직도 그 온전함을 붙들고 있어요? 하나님을 저주하고 죽어 버려요!"
ko.R: 욥의 아내가 욥에게 말했다. "아직도 그 온전함을 놓지 않고 있어요? 하나님을 저주하고 죽어 버려요!"

decisions.choice: curse God: the verb is "bless", meaning "curse"
decisions.reason: As in 1:5, 1:11 and 2:5, the verb for "bless" stands in place of "curse". Some readers have taken it literally, as if she says "bless God, and die", or "say goodbye to God"; but she echoes the satan's very word, and Job's reply (2:10) treats her words as foolish talk.

decisions.choice: still holding fast to your integrity: the LORD's words of 2:3
decisions.reason: She uses the words the LORD used of Job in heaven (2:3). What the LORD praises, she urges him to give up; without knowing it, she presses the satan's case.

decisions.choice: and die: the result of cursing God, or a release from suffering
decisions.reason: Cursing God was a sin punished by death (Leviticus 24:15-16; 1 Kings 21:10, 13). She may mean "curse God, and be put to death", or simply "curse God and be done with it", seeing death as an end to his misery. Either way she counts his life as already lost.

decisions.choice: Job and his wife: "ông" / "bà" (L); "anh" / "em" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Genesis, Literal keeps the formal address of an older couple; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary words between husband and wife.

decisions.choice: Job and his wife speak to each other in 해요체 with "당신" at every level
alternatives: 해라체 for her outburst at Literal
decisions.reason: The ordinary polite style between husband and wife. Her words are harsh, but Korean shows that in the words themselves ("죽어 버려요"), so one speech level holds for both of them through the scene.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֗יהָ כְּדַבֵּ֞ר אַחַ֤ת הַנְּבָלוֹת֙ תְּדַבֵּ֔רִי גַּ֣ם אֶת־הַטּ֗וֹב נְקַבֵּל֙ מֵאֵ֣ת הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְאֶת־הָרָ֖ע לֹ֣א נְקַבֵּ֑ל בְּכָל־זֹ֛את לֹא־חָטָ֥א אִיּ֖וֹב בִּשְׂפָתָֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he said to her, as speaks one of the foolish women you speak. Also the good shall we receive from God, and the evil not shall we receive? In all this not sinned Job with his lips.

en.L: And he said to her, "As one of the foolish women speaks, you speak. Shall we receive the good from God, and not receive the bad?" In all this Job did not sin with his lips.
en.B: He said to her, "You are talking like one of the foolish women. Are we to accept good from God and not accept trouble as well?" In all this Job did not sin in what he said.
en.R: Job answered her, "You are talking like a foolish woman. We accept the good things God gives us. Should we not also accept the hard things?" Through all of this, Job did not say anything sinful.

es.L: Y él le dijo: «Como habla una de las mujeres necias, hablas tú. ¿También lo bueno aceptaremos de Dios, y lo malo no lo aceptaremos?». En todo esto Job no pecó con sus labios.
es.B: Él le respondió: «Hablas como una de esas mujeres necias. ¿Vamos a aceptar de Dios el bien y no aceptar también la desgracia?». En todo esto Job no pecó con lo que dijo.
es.R: Job le contestó: «Hablas como una mujer necia. Aceptamos las cosas buenas que Dios nos da. ¿No debemos aceptar también las cosas difíciles?». En medio de todo esto, Job no dijo nada que fuera pecado.

fr.L: Et il lui dit : « Tu parles comme parle l’une des femmes insensées. Recevrons-nous de Dieu ce qui est bon, et ce qui est mauvais, ne le recevrons-nous pas ? » Dans tout cela, Job ne pécha pas par ses lèvres.
fr.B: Il lui répondit : « Tu parles comme une de ces femmes insensées. Accepterions-nous de Dieu le bonheur, sans accepter aussi le malheur ? » Dans tout cela, Job ne pécha pas en paroles.
fr.R: Job lui a répondu : « Tu parles comme une femme insensée. Nous acceptons les bonnes choses que Dieu nous donne. Ne devrions-nous pas accepter aussi les choses dures ? » Malgré tout cela, Job n’a rien dit qui soit un péché.

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "Unasema kama asemavyo mmoja wa wanawake wapumbavu. Je, hata mema tutayakubali kutoka kwa Mungu, na mabaya hatutayakubali?" Katika haya yote Ayubu hakutenda dhambi kwa midomo yake.
sw.B: Akamwambia, "Unaongea kama mmoja wa wanawake wapumbavu. Je, tukubali mema kutoka kwa Mungu, tusikubali na taabu?" Katika haya yote Ayubu hakutenda dhambi kwa maneno yake.
sw.R: Ayubu akamjibu, "Unaongea kama mwanamke mpumbavu. Tunakubali mambo mazuri ambayo Mungu anatupa. Je, hatupaswi kukubali pia mambo magumu?" Katika yote hayo, Ayubu hakusema neno lolote la dhambi.

vi.L: Và ông nói với bà: "Như một trong những người đàn bà ngu dại nói, bà cũng nói vậy. Chúng ta cũng nhận điều lành từ Đức Chúa Trời, mà điều dữ lại không nhận sao?" Trong mọi việc ấy, Gióp không phạm tội bằng môi miệng mình.
vi.B: Ông nói với vợ: "Em nói như một người đàn bà dại dột. Chúng ta nhận phước lành từ Đức Chúa Trời, lẽ nào lại không nhận cả tai họa?" Trong mọi điều ấy, Gióp không phạm tội trong lời nói.
vi.R: Gióp đáp: "Em nói như một người đàn bà dại dột. Chúng ta nhận những điều tốt Đức Chúa Trời ban cho. Lẽ nào chúng ta không nhận cả những điều khó khăn sao?" Qua mọi chuyện ấy, Gióp không nói điều gì tội lỗi.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 아내에게 말했다. "당신은 어리석은 여자들 가운데 하나가 말하듯 말하는군요. 우리가 하나님께 좋은 것도 받는데, 나쁜 것은 받지 않겠어요?" 이 모든 일에도 욥은 자기 입술로 죄를 짓지 않았다.
ko.B: 욥이 아내에게 말했다. "당신은 어리석은 여자들처럼 말하는군요. 우리가 하나님께 복을 받았는데, 재앙은 받지 않겠다는 말이에요?" 이 모든 일에도 욥은 말로 죄를 짓지 않았다.
ko.R: 욥이 대답했다. "당신은 어리석은 여자처럼 말하는군요. 우리는 하나님께서 주시는 좋은 것을 받아요. 그렇다면 힘든 일도 받아야 하지 않겠어요?" 이 모든 일을 겪으면서도 욥은 죄가 되는 말을 하나도 하지 않았다.

decisions.choice: foolish: godless in thought and speech, not lacking intelligence
decisions.reason: The word for a fool in Hebrew means one who acts or speaks without regard for God and what is right (Psalm 14:1; 1 Samuel 25:25; Isaiah 32:6). Job does not call his wife a fool; he says she is talking the way such women talk.

decisions.choice: the good and the bad: blessing and misfortune
decisions.reason: The second word is the one translated "evil" in 1:1, but here it means harm or misfortune, what happens to a person, not wrongdoing (as in Isaiah 45:7; Amos 3:6). Job accepts both prosperity and trouble as coming from God.

decisions.choice: Job did not sin with his lips: his words were without fault
decisions.reason: The verdict matches 1:22 and answers the satan's claim that Job would curse God "to your face" (2:5), that is, in speech. The phrase stresses what he said; some later readers took it to hint at sinful thoughts within, but the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: the bad (Literal); trouble (Balanced); the hard things (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Evil" in English suggests wickedness, which is not the sense here; each level uses a word for misfortune.

decisions.choice: two sentences for the question (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable states the first half as a fact and keeps only the second as a question, which shows plainly what Job is arguing.

source.text: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֞וּ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת׀רֵעֵ֣י אִיּ֗וֹב אֵ֣ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֣ה הַזֹּאת֮ הַבָּ֣אָה עָלָיו֒ וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִמְּקֹמ֔וֹ אֱלִיפַ֤ז הַתֵּימָנִי֙ וּבִלְדַּ֣ד הַשּׁוּחִ֔י וְצוֹפַ֖ר הַנַּֽעֲמָתִ֑י וַיִּוָּעֲד֣וּ יַחְדָּ֔ו לָב֥וֹא לָנֽוּד־ל֖וֹ וּֽלְנַחֲמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard [the] three friends of Job all this evil that had come on him, and they came each from his place, Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite; and they met by appointment together to come to show sympathy to him and to comfort him.

en.L: And the three friends of Job heard of all this evil that had come on him, and they came, each from his own place, Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite; and they arranged together to come to show him sympathy and to comfort him.
en.B: When Job's three friends, Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite, heard about all the trouble that had come on him, they set out, each from his own home. They had agreed to meet and go together to show him sympathy and comfort him.
en.R: Job had three friends: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite. When they heard about all the terrible things that had happened to Job, each of them left his home. They agreed to meet and go together to visit Job, to share his grief and to comfort him.

es.L: Y los tres amigos de Job oyeron todo este mal que había venido sobre él, y vinieron cada uno de su lugar, Elifaz el temanita, Bildad el suhita y Zofar el naamatita; y se pusieron de acuerdo para venir juntos a mostrarle su compasión y a consolarlo.
es.B: Cuando los tres amigos de Job, Elifaz el temanita, Bildad el suhita y Zofar el naamatita, se enteraron de todas las desgracias que le habían sobrevenido, salieron cada uno de su casa. Se habían puesto de acuerdo para encontrarse e ir juntos a acompañarlo en su dolor y consolarlo.
es.R: Job tenía tres amigos: Elifaz el temanita, Bildad el suhita y Zofar el naamatita. Cuando supieron todas las cosas terribles que le habían pasado a Job, cada uno salió de su casa. Se pusieron de acuerdo para encontrarse e ir juntos a visitar a Job, para acompañarlo en su dolor y consolarlo.

fr.L: Et les trois amis de Job apprirent tout ce mal qui était venu sur lui, et ils vinrent chacun de son lieu, Éliphaz le Témanite, Bildad le Shouhite et Tsophar le Naamatite ; et ils se donnèrent rendez-vous pour venir ensemble lui témoigner leur compassion et le consoler.
fr.B: Quand les trois amis de Job, Éliphaz le Témanite, Bildad le Shouhite et Tsophar le Naamatite, apprirent tous les malheurs qui lui étaient arrivés, ils partirent chacun de chez soi. Ils s’étaient mis d’accord pour se retrouver et aller ensemble lui montrer leur compassion et le consoler.
fr.R: Job avait trois amis : Éliphaz le Témanite, Bildad le Shouhite et Tsophar le Naamatite. Quand ils ont appris toutes les choses terribles qui étaient arrivées à Job, chacun d’eux a quitté sa maison. Ils se sont mis d’accord pour se retrouver et aller ensemble rendre visite à Job, pour partager sa peine et le consoler.

sw.L: Na rafiki watatu wa Ayubu walisikia habari ya mabaya haya yote yaliyompata, wakaja kila mmoja kutoka mahali pake, Elifazi Mtemani, Bildadi Mshua na Sofari Mnaamathi; wakapatana pamoja kuja kumhurumia na kumfariji.
sw.B: Rafiki watatu wa Ayubu, Elifazi Mtemani, Bildadi Mshua na Sofari Mnaamathi, waliposikia juu ya taabu zote zilizompata, waliondoka kila mmoja nyumbani kwake. Walikuwa wamepatana kukutana na kwenda pamoja kumwonea huruma na kumfariji.
sw.R: Ayubu alikuwa na rafiki watatu: Elifazi Mtemani, Bildadi Mshua na Sofari Mnaamathi. Waliposikia mambo yote mabaya yaliyompata Ayubu, kila mmoja wao aliondoka nyumbani kwake. Walipatana kukutana na kwenda pamoja kumtembelea Ayubu, ili kuomboleza pamoja naye na kumfariji.

vi.L: Và ba bạn của Gióp nghe về mọi điều dữ này đã đến trên ông, thì họ đến, mỗi người từ chỗ mình, Ê-li-pha người Thê-man, Binh-đát người Su-ách và Sô-pha người Na-a-ma; và họ hẹn nhau cùng đến để chia buồn với ông và an ủi ông.
vi.B: Khi ba người bạn của Gióp là Ê-li-pha người Thê-man, Binh-đát người Su-ách và Sô-pha người Na-a-ma nghe biết mọi tai họa đã xảy đến cho ông, thì mỗi người rời nhà mình ra đi. Họ đã hẹn gặp nhau để cùng đến chia buồn và an ủi ông.
vi.R: Gióp có ba người bạn: Ê-li-pha người Thê-man, Binh-đát người Su-ách và Sô-pha người Na-a-ma. Khi nghe biết mọi chuyện khủng khiếp đã xảy đến cho Gióp, mỗi người đều rời nhà mình. Họ hẹn gặp nhau để cùng đi thăm Gióp, chia sẻ nỗi đau với ông và an ủi ông.

ko.L: 그리고 욥의 세 친구가 그에게 닥친 이 모든 재앙을 듣고, 각자 자기 처소에서 왔다. 곧 데만 사람 엘리바스와 수아 사람 빌닷과 나아마 사람 소발이었다. 그들은 함께 가서 그와 함께 슬퍼하고 그를 위로하려고 서로 약속하였다.
ko.B: 욥의 세 친구, 곧 데만 사람 엘리바스와 수아 사람 빌닷과 나아마 사람 소발은 욥에게 닥친 모든 재앙을 전해 듣고 저마다 자기 집을 떠났다. 그들은 만나서 함께 가서 욥과 함께 슬퍼하고 그를 위로하기로 약속했던 것이다.
ko.R: 욥에게는 데만 사람 엘리바스와 수아 사람 빌닷과 나아마 사람 소발이라는 세 친구가 있었다. 그들은 욥에게 끔찍한 일들이 일어났다는 소식을 듣고 저마다 집을 떠났다. 그들은 한곳에서 만나 함께 욥을 찾아가 그의 슬픔을 함께 나누고 위로하기로 약속했다.

decisions.choice: the Temanite, the Shuhite, the Naamathite: men from lands east and southeast of Israel
decisions.reason: Teman was a region of Edom known for its wise men (Jeremiah 49:7; Obadiah 9), and Teman is the name of a grandson of Esau (Genesis 36:11). Shuah was a son of Abraham and Keturah whose descendants were sent to the east (Genesis 25:2, 6). Where Naamah lay is not known. Like Job, the friends are wise men of the East.

decisions.choice: to show sympathy: to grieve with him
decisions.reason: The verb means to move the head back and forth, a gesture of sympathy, and so to console, to share in grief (42:11; Jeremiah 16:5; 22:10).

decisions.choice: they met by appointment: they arranged to meet
decisions.reason: The verb means to meet at an agreed time and place (Amos 3:3). The friends came from far away and planned the visit together, a sign of their real care for Job.

decisions.choice: evil (Literal); trouble (Balanced); terrible things (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2:10, the word means misfortune here, not wickedness; Literal keeps the Hebrew word's double sense.

decisions.choice: "Elifaz el temanita, Bildad el suhita y Zofar el naamatita"
decisions.reason: The friends' names in their Spanish Bible forms, the same through the book; the people names are lowercase, as Spanish writes them.

decisions.choice: "Éliphaz le Témanite, Bildad le Shouhite et Tsophar le Naamatite"
decisions.reason: The friends' names in one French form through the book, following the published spellings of Teman and Shouah.

decisions.choice: "Elifazi Mtemani, Bildadi Mshua na Sofari Mnaamathi"
decisions.reason: The friends' names in one Swahili form through the book, with the people names formed with "M-" as Swahili does.

decisions.reason: The friends' names in the traditional Vietnamese forms, the same through the book.

decisions.choice: Job and his friends say "anh" / "các anh" and "tôi" to each other
decisions.reason: Old friends of equal standing; the familiar but respectful "anh" holds at every level through the dialogues.

decisions.choice: "데만 사람 엘리바스", "수아 사람 빌닷", "나아마 사람 소발"
decisions.reason: Korean puts the place before the name; the forms are the same through the book.

source.text: וַיִּשְׂא֨וּ אֶת־עֵינֵיהֶ֤ם מֵרָחוֹק֙ וְלֹ֣א הִכִּירֻ֔הוּ וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם וַיִּבְכּ֑וּ וַֽיִּקְרְעוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מְעִל֔וֹ וַיִּזְרְק֥וּ עָפָ֛ר עַל־רָאשֵׁיהֶ֖ם הַשָּׁמָֽיְמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they lifted up their eyes from a distance and not they recognized him, and they lifted up their voice and wept; and they tore each his robe and threw dust on their heads toward the heavens.

en.L: And they lifted up their eyes from a distance and did not recognize him; and they lifted up their voices and wept, and they tore each one his robe and threw dust on their heads toward the heavens.
en.B: When they saw him from a distance, they did not recognize him. They wept aloud, and each of them tore his robe, and they threw dust into the air onto their heads.
en.R: When they saw him from far away, they did not recognize him. They cried loudly. Each of them tore his robe, and they threw dust into the air so that it fell on their heads.

es.L: Y alzaron sus ojos desde lejos y no lo reconocieron; y alzaron su voz y lloraron, y rasgaron cada uno su manto y echaron polvo sobre sus cabezas hacia los cielos.
es.B: Cuando lo vieron de lejos, no lo reconocieron. Lloraron a gritos, cada uno rasgó su manto y lanzaron polvo al aire sobre sus cabezas.
es.R: Cuando lo vieron de lejos, no lo reconocieron. Lloraron con fuerza. Cada uno rasgó su manto, y echaron polvo al aire para que les cayera sobre la cabeza.

fr.L: Et ils levèrent les yeux de loin, et ils ne le reconnurent pas ; et ils élevèrent la voix et pleurèrent, et ils déchirèrent chacun son manteau et jetèrent de la poussière sur leurs têtes vers les cieux.
fr.B: Quand ils l’aperçurent de loin, ils ne le reconnurent pas. Ils éclatèrent en sanglots, chacun déchira son manteau, et ils lancèrent de la poussière en l’air, sur leurs têtes.
fr.R: Quand ils l’ont vu de loin, ils ne l’ont pas reconnu. Ils ont pleuré très fort. Chacun a déchiré son manteau, et ils ont lancé de la poussière en l’air pour qu’elle retombe sur leur tête.

sw.L: Nao walipoinua macho yao kwa mbali hawakumtambua; wakapaza sauti zao wakalia, wakapasua kila mmoja joho lake, wakarusha mavumbi juu ya vichwa vyao kuelekea mbinguni.
sw.B: Walipomwona kwa mbali hawakumtambua. Wakalia kwa sauti kuu, kila mmoja akalipasua joho lake, nao wakarusha mavumbi hewani juu ya vichwa vyao.
sw.R: Walipomwona kwa mbali, hawakumtambua. Wakalia kwa sauti kubwa. Kila mmoja akalipasua joho lake, nao wakarusha mavumbi hewani yakawaangukia vichwani.

vi.L: Và họ ngước mắt lên từ đằng xa mà không nhận ra ông; và họ cất tiếng lên mà khóc, và mỗi người xé áo choàng mình, và tung bụi lên đầu mình hướng về trời.
vi.B: Khi nhìn thấy ông từ xa, họ không nhận ra ông. Họ khóc lớn tiếng, mỗi người xé áo choàng mình, rồi tung bụi lên trời cho rơi xuống đầu mình.
vi.R: Khi thấy ông từ xa, họ không nhận ra ông. Họ khóc thật lớn. Mỗi người xé áo choàng của mình, rồi tung bụi lên trời cho rơi xuống đầu.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 멀리서 눈을 들었으나 그를 알아보지 못했다. 그들은 목소리를 높여 울었고, 각자 자기 겉옷을 찢고, 하늘을 향해 티끌을 자기들의 머리 위에 뿌렸다.
ko.B: 그들은 멀리서 욥을 보았으나 그를 알아보지 못했다. 그들은 소리 내어 울며 저마다 겉옷을 찢고, 티끌을 공중에 날려 자기들 머리 위에 뒤집어썼다.
ko.R: 그들은 멀리서 욥을 보았지만 알아보지 못했다. 그들은 큰 소리로 울었다. 저마다 겉옷을 찢고, 흙먼지를 공중에 뿌려 머리에 떨어지게 했다.

decisions.choice: tore their robes and threw dust on their heads: mourning as for the dead
decisions.reason: Tearing clothes and putting dust or earth on the head were signs of deep grief (Joshua 7:6; 1 Samuel 4:12; 2 Samuel 1:2; Lamentations 2:10). Throwing it "toward the heavens" so that it fell on them seems to have been part of the rite. The friends mourn Job as if he were already dead.

decisions.choice: lifted up their eyes; lifted up their voices: looked; wept aloud
decisions.reason: Both are common Hebrew expressions: "lift up the eyes" means to look (Genesis 22:4), and "lift up the voice and weep" means to cry aloud (Ruth 1:9).

decisions.choice: did not recognize him: his disease had changed him beyond recognition
decisions.reason: The text says they did not know him, which shows how terribly the sores had changed his appearance (compare 19:19-20).

decisions.choice: saw him; wept aloud (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the two idioms; Literal keeps them.

source.text: וַיֵּשְׁב֤וּ אִתּוֹ֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים וְשִׁבְעַ֣ת לֵיל֑וֹת וְאֵין־דֹּבֵ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ דָּבָ֔ר כִּ֣י רָא֔וּ כִּֽי־גָדַ֥ל הַכְּאֵ֖ב מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And they sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and there was none speaking to him a word, for they saw that great [was] the pain very.

en.L: And they sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that the pain was very great.
en.B: Then they sat with him on the ground for seven days and seven nights. No one said a word to him, because they saw how great his suffering was.
en.R: Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights. None of them said a word to him, because they could see how much he was suffering.

es.L: Y se sentaron junto a él en el suelo siete días y siete noches, y no hubo quien le dijera una palabra, porque vieron que el dolor era grandísimo.
es.B: Luego se sentaron en el suelo con él durante siete días y siete noches. Ninguno le dijo una sola palabra, porque veían cuán grande era su sufrimiento.
es.R: Después se sentaron en el suelo con él durante siete días y siete noches. Ninguno le dijo nada, porque se daban cuenta de lo mucho que estaba sufriendo.

fr.L: Et ils s’assirent avec lui à terre sept jours et sept nuits, et personne ne lui dit une parole, car ils voyaient que la douleur était très grande.
fr.B: Puis ils restèrent assis à terre avec lui pendant sept jours et sept nuits. Aucun ne lui adressa la parole, car ils voyaient à quel point sa souffrance était immense.
fr.R: Ensuite, ils se sont assis par terre avec lui pendant sept jours et sept nuits. Aucun d’eux ne lui a dit un mot, parce qu’ils voyaient bien qu’il souffrait énormément.

sw.L: Wakaketi pamoja naye ardhini siku saba na usiku saba, na hakuna aliyesema naye neno, kwa sababu waliona kwamba uchungu ulikuwa mkubwa sana.
sw.B: Kisha wakaketi chini pamoja naye kwa siku saba mchana na usiku. Hakuna aliyemwambia neno lolote, kwa sababu waliona jinsi mateso yake yalivyokuwa makubwa.
sw.R: Kisha wakaketi chini pamoja naye kwa siku saba, mchana na usiku. Hakuna hata mmoja aliyemwambia neno, kwa sababu waliona jinsi alivyokuwa akiteseka sana.

vi.L: Và họ ngồi xuống đất cùng ông suốt bảy ngày và bảy đêm, chẳng có ai nói với ông một lời, vì họ thấy nỗi đau quá lớn.
vi.B: Rồi họ ngồi trên đất với ông suốt bảy ngày bảy đêm. Không ai nói với ông một lời nào, vì họ thấy nỗi thống khổ của ông quá lớn.
vi.R: Rồi họ ngồi bệt xuống đất bên ông suốt bảy ngày bảy đêm. Không ai nói với ông câu nào, vì họ thấy ông đau khổ quá nhiều.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 이레 낮과 이레 밤을 그와 함께 땅에 앉아 있었는데, 그에게 한마디 말을 하는 자가 없었다. 고통이 매우 큰 것을 그들이 보았기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러고는 이레 밤낮을 그와 함께 땅바닥에 앉아 있었다. 욥이 겪는 고통이 너무나 큰 것을 보았기에, 아무도 그에게 한마디도 하지 못했다.
ko.R: 그들은 칠 일 밤낮을 욥과 함께 땅바닥에 앉아 있었다. 욥이 얼마나 고통스러워하는지 보았기 때문에, 아무도 그에게 말 한마디 하지 않았다.

decisions.choice: sat on the ground seven days and seven nights: the full time of mourning
decisions.reason: Seven days was the time of mourning for the dead (Genesis 50:10; 1 Samuel 31:13), and sitting on the ground was a mourner's posture (Lamentations 2:10; Ezekiel 26:16). Ezekiel sat seven days in silent distress among the exiles (Ezekiel 3:15).

decisions.choice: the pain: suffering of body and spirit
decisions.reason: The word is used of physical pain (16:6; Genesis 34:25) and of grief of heart (Isaiah 65:14). Both are meant here.

decisions.choice: no one spoke a word: the silence that ends when Job speaks first
decisions.reason: The friends wait in silence, as was fitting for comforters, until Job himself breaks it with his curse on the day of his birth (3:1). The prose story now gives way to the poetry of the speeches.

decisions.choice: pain (Literal); suffering (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Suffering" covers both the bodily pain and the grief the word means here.
